title: Common mobile artifacts: chats, calls, location
quick: Mobile artifacts are traces left by apps and the system, such as chats, call logs, contacts, photos and location data. They help build a picture of what a user did and when.

sections.title: Main groups
text: Common artifacts are messages and chats, call history, contacts, photos and videos with metadata, browser history, app usage, installed apps, Wi-Fi networks and location data. Each can support a part of a story, but none proves intent alone.
points: Communications: SMS, chat apps, calls, email.
Media: photos, videos and their metadata.
Location: GPS points, Wi-Fi and cell data, saved places.

sections.title: Where they live
text: Most are stored in app databases and files. Their paths and layouts depend on the app and the operating system version, so check current documentation or test on a known device. Parsers read these locations and build a report, but you should know how to check key results by hand.

sections.title: Time and context
text: Timestamps use different formats and time zones. Location points may be approximate. Treat an artifact as a clue, compare several sources and report how sure you are.

example: A student parses a practice phone image with ALEAPP. The report shows a chat, a call and a photo within the same five minutes. They check the time zone, open the databases to confirm the rows, and then add the three events to a timeline.
mistakes: Trusting a parser report without checking the raw data.
Ignoring time zones and time formats.
Treating a location point as exact.
Missing artifacts from a new app version.
Reporting one artifact as proof of what a user meant.

terms.meaning: A trace left on a device by a user, an app or the system.
Data about data, such as the time a photo was taken.
A tool that reads a file format and turns it into readable data.
A recorded date and time value.

exam.q: Why are timestamps a common problem in mobile forensics?
exam.a: Apps use different formats and time zones, so an unchecked conversion can give the wrong time.

exam.q: What should you do besides running a parser?
exam.a: Check important findings against the raw data or another source and record your method.
